A 32 years old G2P1 female presents to her obstetrician with abdominal discomfort, increased back pain, shortness of breath, and swelling in her feet and ankles.
Ultrasound reveals an amniotic fluid index (AFI) of 27 cm. The condition is caused by which of the following?

options.label: C
options.text: Precocious development of the swallowing reflex in the fetus

questions.solution: An amniotic fluid index of 27 cm is indicative of polyhydramnios. Duodenal and/or esophageal atresia result in an inability of the fetus to swallow amniotic fluid. The result is that normal recirculation of amniotic fluid through the embryo is greatly reduced or eliminated, causing an excess of amniotic fluid. Low volumes of amniotic fluid (oligohydramnios) are caused by rupture of the fetal membranes, bilateral agenesis of the kidneys, or obstructive uropathy. Hypoplasia of the lungs and compression of the umbilical cord are associated with oligohydramnios, but do not cause it. Less urine output = less amniotic fluid; less swallowing = more amniotic fluid. @Neet_pg_bot
questions.solutionHtml:
• An amniotic fluid index of 27 cm is indicative of polyhydramnios.
  • Duodenal and/or esophageal atresia result in an inability of the fetus to swallow amniotic fluid.
  • The result is that normal recirculation of amniotic fluid through the embryo is greatly reduced or eliminated, causing an excess of amniotic fluid.
  • Low volumes of amniotic fluid (oligohydramnios) are caused by rupture of the fetal membranes, bilateral agenesis of the kidneys, or obstructive uropathy.
  • Hypoplasia of the lungs and compression of the umbilical cord are associated with oligohydramnios, but do not cause it.
  • Less urine output = less amniotic fluid; less swallowing = more amniotic fluid.

questions.stem: A woman is 24 weeks pregnant with her first child. She developed cellulitis in the right leg and requires antibiotic treatment. Which of the following antibiotics should not be used during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy?
questions.stemHtml: A woman is 24 weeks pregnant with her first child. She developed cellulitis in the right leg and requires antibiotic treatment. Which of the following antibiotics should not be used during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy?
questions.solution: The FDA has a classification system that designates the safety of drugs in pregnancy. Class A Safety of the drug without effects on the fetus. No antibiotic is designated as a class A drug in pregnancy. Class B No effects in animal reproduction, or if the animal data show effects, adequate data in pregnant women to show these drugs can be safely used. Antibitoics include azithromycin, cephalosporins, clindamycin, meropenem, penicillins, and vancomycin. Class C More potential risks, but one has to determine if the potential benefits to the health of the mother warrant use despite the potential risk. Antibiotics include fluoroquinolones and linezolid. Class D Some degree of fetal risk and should be avoided if other safer alternatives exist. Antibitoics include Sulfonamides and tetracyclines The specific concern for use of doxycycline in the second and third trimester is discoloration of the teeth in the fetus. @Neet_pg_bot
questions.solutionHtml:
The FDA has a classification system that designates the safety of drugs in pregnancy.

Class A

  • Safety of the drug without effects on the fetus.
  • No antibiotic is designated as a class A drug in pregnancy.

Class B

  • No effects in animal reproduction, or if the animal data show effects, adequate data in pregnant women to show these drugs can be safely used.
  • Antibitoics include azithromycin, cephalosporins, clindamycin, meropenem, penicillins, and vancomycin.

Class C

  • More potential risks, but one has to determine if the potential benefits to the health of the mother warrant use despite the potential risk.
  • Antibiotics include fluoroquinolones and linezolid.

Class D

  • Some degree of fetal risk and should be avoided if other safer alternatives exist.
  • Antibitoics include Sulfonamides and tetracyclines
  • The specific concern for use of doxycycline in the second and third trimester is discoloration of the teeth in the fetus.

questions.stemHtml: A 16 week pregnant 24 year-old woman is seen for routine follow-up of an uncomplicated pregnancy. What is the recommended screening and treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria in this particular patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Screen and treated in 3rd trimester only.

options.label: B
options.text: Screened with urine culture, not treated unless symptomatic.

options.label: C
options.text: Screened at 16wks and treated if culture is positive.

questions.answerText: Screened at 16wks and treated if culture is positive.
questions.solution: Asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB): without local or systemic symptoms of infection presents with bacteria in the urine diagnostic cutoff: >105 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL in spontaneously voiding patients >102 CFU/mL in catheterized individuals who have a catheter. In pregnant women: screening and treatment of ASB recommended due to increased risk of: preterm birth perinatal death of fetus pyelonephritis in mother. @Neet_pg_bot
questions.solutionHtml:
• Asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB):
    • without local or systemic symptoms of infection
    • presents with bacteria in the urine
    • diagnostic cutoff:
      • >105 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL in spontaneously voiding patients
      • >102 CFU/mL in catheterized individuals who have a catheter.
    • In pregnant women: screening and treatment of ASB recommended due to increased risk of:
      • preterm birth
      • perinatal death of fetus
      • pyelonephritis in mother.
